fields.title: Tracing and how to read it
fields.keyTakeaway: Tracing answers three product questions—why sequential, why this call, why so many—and the answers usually yield more than code optimization.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: There is a tool that shows a request path across all services. What does a PM see in it?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: [[distributed-tracing|Tracing]] is usually there and usually unused by the product. At the same time, it answers product questions faster than any discussion: where the time goes, what can be parallelized, which call is redundant.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Tracing shows the request path as a sequence of segments: each call with its own start time and duration. Read like a Gantt chart.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: What a PM can see without technical knowledge:
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **What is sequential and what is parallel.** Segments one after another mean waiting. If there is no dependency between them, they can be run in parallel—and this is usually the cheapest win.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **What takes the most time.** The longest segment. Often an unexpected component.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **What is called repeatedly.** Twenty identical short segments—the classic [[n1-problem|N+1 problem]]: requesting a list triggers a request for each item.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **What is called in vain.** A segment whose result is not used on this screen. Happens more often than you think—usually a legacy of past versions.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: Three questions a PM can ask based on tracing:
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: *Why are these two calls sequential?* *Why is this call here?* *Why are there twenty of them instead of one?*
fields.sections/2/blocks/8/text: All three regularly lead to time savings without any code optimization.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Checkout tracing yielded three findings in an hour.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: *Promo code verification always ran,* even when there was no promo code. 180 ms per checkout wasted. Fix—one hour.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: *Stock checks were done with one request per item.* Twelve items—twelve sequential calls, 480 ms. Batch request—60 ms.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: *Recommendations service call* for "similar products" on the confirmation screen. The block was removed from the screen half a year ago, but the call remained. 140 ms.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Total 740 ms out of 1,600, without a single line of code optimized. Only removing the unnecessary and batching.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Tracing shows where the time goes, but not why. A slow database query is visible as a segment, but the cause — a missing index — requires a different tool.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Tracing answers three product questions—why sequential, why this call, why so many—and the answers usually yield more than code optimization.
